latest_findings.claim: Halving lr from 0.001 to 0.0005 (N=64, e in [0, 0.85], seeds 59-61, best-of-5 controls) delays accel_step formation only slightly. Read from the trajectories, the 0.1-bar margin is first crossed and held at steps 70 (seed 59), 80 (seed 60) and 100 (seed 61), compared with 60/60/70 at lr=0.001. That is +10/+20/+30 steps rather than the roughly 2x (>= 100 in all seeds) that proportional scaling predicts. Final accel_step R2 is 0.49-0.59 at layer 4 vs controls 0.25-0.33, margin 0.244-0.257. Force never beats its control: R2 0.22-0.28 vs 0.15-0.21, margin 0.065-0.078. All runs beat the baseline (val_mse_ratio 0.214-0.224).
latest_findings.confidence_note: The pre-registered false condition holds: 2 of 3 seeds are at step <= 90 and within 20 steps of lr=0.001. The undertraining escape does not apply, since all final margins are >= 0.24. The hypothesis's 60/60/70 baseline is assumed to belong to seeds 59/60/61. Under any assignment of those values, at least 2 seeds are still within 20 steps, so the verdict does not depend on that assumption. Lowering lr did slow training: final val_mse_ratio is about 0.22 here against about 0.13 at lr=0.001. Seed 61 (+30) is also the one seed that moved as much as predicted. So formation is not independent of lr. It shifts sub-proportionally, and the result rules out 'set by cumulative lr*steps' rather than 'unaffected by the optimizer'. Half-final-margin steps here are 100/90/110 (seeds 59/60/61). The seed-matched lr=0.001 half-final values are not in this record, so that half of the expected-if-true criterion cannot be checked here. The 10-step checkpoint spacing limits resolution to about ±10 steps. The verdict would weaken if the lr=0.001 trajectories for seeds 59-61 give formation steps of 50 or earlier, or if a lr=0.00025 arm shows formation scaling steeply. probes_final.formed_at_step matches the trajectory in all 3 runs, so there is no off-by-one lag here.

latest_findings.claim: At N=256 and e in [0, 0.5] (seeds 62-64), accel_step crosses the persistent 0.1 margin bar at steps 100, 100 and 110 and reaches half its final margin at steps 90, 100 and 110. The matched N=64 arm crossed the 0.1 bar at steps 90-100, so the N=256 delay is only 0-20 steps, not the >=20 steps in every seed that the hypothesis predicted. The half-final delay is +30 for seed 62 (90 vs 60) but only +10 for seed 63 (100 vs 90). Final accel_step R2 is 0.862-0.883 against controls of 0.674-0.705 (margins 0.177-0.187, all at layer 4). Force does not beat its control at the end (R2 0.18-0.59, margins 0.004-0.030) after an early transient margin of 0.145-0.165 at steps 10-20 that fades to about 0 by step 110. val_mse_ratio is 12.0-13.3, so no seed beats the baseline.
latest_findings.confidence_note: The expected-if-true outcome failed: the 0.1-bar gap is at most 20 steps and is below 20 in at least two seeds, so the seeds 56-58 result (+20/+70/+30) did not replicate cleanly. The expected-if-false outcome (half-final gap <= 10 in at least 2 of 3 seeds) is met only by seed 63; seed 62 is +30. Seed 64's N=64 half-final step was not available to me (the N=64 finding file could not be read). If it is >= 100, the gap is <= 10 and the verdict becomes refuted; otherwise the result stays mixed. The N=64 values here come from summaries quoted in the open questions, not from per-seed trajectories, so the paired differences should be recomputed from the N=64 trajectories. The control-ceiling explanation does not fit this pair: N=256 final margins (0.177-0.187) are higher than the N=64 margins (0.144-0.160 in seeds 62-63), yet N=256 still crosses no earlier. Checkpoints are 10 steps apart, so differences of 10 steps are at the resolution limit. All three N=256 runs completed (300/300 steps), and formed_at_step matches the trajectory in every run.

latest_findings.claim: At N=64, e in [0, 0.5], seeds 62-64 all landed inside both predicted windows when read from the per-checkpoint trajectory. The accel_step margin first held at or above the 0.1 bar for good at step 90 (seed 64), 100 (seed 62) and 100 (seed 63), and first reached half its final margin at steps 80, 60 and 90. Final accel_step R2 was 0.890-0.902 at layer 4 against controls of 0.724-0.746 (margins 0.144-0.167). Force never beat its control: final margins were 0.033-0.080 against a 0.1 bar, after a brief step-10 rise to 0.148-0.159 that fell to about 0 by step 40. So per-snapshot acceleration is decodable, but physical force is not.
latest_findings.confidence_note: All 3 completed seeds fall in both windows. This is a clean result, but 2 of the 6 values sit on a window edge: seed 62 and seed 63 both have persistent step 100, the upper bound, and seed 63's half-final step is 90, also the upper bound. With 10-step checkpoints, a one-checkpoint shift would have put seed 62 or 63 outside, so the windows only just hold. The half-final measure spreads more (60-90) than the persistent 0.1-bar measure (90-100). That is partly because seed 62 has the lowest final margin, 0.144, and so the lowest half-final threshold. Here formed_at_step equals the trajectory value in every run (90, 100, 100), so the earlier one-checkpoint lag did not recur. Formation comes while val_mse_ratio is still 1.7-2.1, about 2.0-2.9% of each run's step-0 value, and 40-60 steps before the model beats the baseline (steps 140-160). Distance forms at steps 10-20, which is 70-90 steps before accel_step. Raw accel_step controls are high (0.72-0.75), which caps the margin. A paired N=256 arm with persistent steps also at or below 100 would mean this reference cannot separate the arms. Persistent steps above 100 in a fresh seed at N=64 would mean the window is too narrow.

latest_findings.claim: At e in [0, 0.85] and N=256, accel_step forms at the same training step in all 3 seeds. Read from the trajectory, the margin first holds at >= 0.1 at steps 60, 70 and 60 (seeds 59, 60, 61), and reaches half its final margin at step 70 in every seed. The paired N=64 arm formed at steps 60-70, so the N=256 minus N=64 gap is at most about 10 steps. Final accel_step margins are 0.268, 0.210 and 0.226 at layer 4 (R2 0.46-0.62 vs controls 0.24-0.35), while force never clears the bar (margin 0.004-0.031). This happens even though N=256 never beats constant-velocity extrapolation (final val_mse_ratio 2.03-2.37).
latest_findings.confidence_note: All 3 seeds trained to 600/600 steps. Checkpoints are 10 steps apart, so a gap of 10 or less is at the resolution limit. The N=64 comparison uses the 60-70 range reported for the paired arm (exp-20261012-032843-c3f5, f-20261012-034018-5526). I did not re-derive the N=64 half-final-margin step for each seed here. It is very likely within 20 steps, because those margins rise steeply after step 60, but it should be checked from those trajectories. Seed 61 crosses at exactly 0.100 at step 60, so its 0.1-bar step could fairly be called 70. That still falls within 20 steps. Here formed_at_step matches the trajectory in all 3 runs, so the lag raised in q-20261012-032843-df65 does not show up. Formation happens at about 15-18% of step-0 val MSE (val_mse_ratio 59-68), against about 8-10% at N=64. So timing follows a training-step window, not relative loss reduction. Two things would change the verdict: the N=64 half-margin steps turning out to be >= 90 in 2 or more seeds, or a re-run at finer checkpoint spacing showing a consistent gap of 20 or more steps.

latest_findings.claim: At e in [0, 0.85] and N=64 (4 layers, d_model=64, m2 in [0.1, 1]), all 3 seeds match every expected-if-true condition. Final accel_step R2 at layer 4 is 0.594, 0.570 and 0.507 against best-of-5 controls of 0.333, 0.282 and 0.248, giving margins of 0.261, 0.287 and 0.258 (control_spread 0.017-0.022). Persistent 0.1-bar formation steps read from the trajectory are 60, 60 and 70, and half-final-margin steps are 70, 80 and 90, so the two measures differ by 10-20 steps. Force is far weaker: final R2 0.25-0.32 against controls 0.16-0.21, margin 0.094-0.112, clearing the bar only in seed 59 at step 400. Headroom-normalized margin is 0.34-0.40 for accel_step and 0.11-0.14 for force.
latest_findings.confidence_note: All 3 seeds (59, 60, 61) completed 600/600 steps and meet each criterion with room to spare. The tightest margins are a final margin of 0.258 against the 0.20 floor and a formation gap of 20 against the 30 limit. In these runs probes_final.formed_at_step (60/60/70) matches the trajectory, so the off-by-one in q-20261012-032843-df65 does not affect them. There are four limits. (1) The larger margin comes from lower controls, not better decoding. Raw accel_step R2 is only 0.51-0.59, well below the 0.85-0.95 seen at e <= 0.5, so 'not capped' means more headroom, not a stronger representation. Linear probes still miss much of the accel_step variance at high e. (2) The e <= 0.5 comparison (controls 0.71-0.77, margins 0.12-0.17) comes from earlier experiments. If those used a different m2 range or seeds, the drop in control R2 cannot be credited to eccentricity alone. (3) Formation at steps 60-70 happens at val_mse_ratio 2.2-2.7, about 8-10% of each run's step-0 value, not the 2-3% seen at e <= 0.5. So the 'fixed fraction of step-0 loss' account of formation does not carry over across eccentricity ranges. (4) Final val_mse_ratio is 0.13, still falling at step 600, so final margins and the half-final step could shift with longer training. Two things would change the verdict: a matched e <= 0.5 arm with the same m2 range and seeds showing similarly low controls, or longer training moving the half-final-margin step more than 30 steps from the 0.1-bar step.
